**Brightcom Group – inflated profits, impairment delays, preferential-issue irregularities**
- SEBI ordered a forensic audit (FY15–FY20) in March 2022 — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/news-cm/sebi-orders-forensic-audit-of-brightcom-group-122030100275_1.html)
- SEBI found profits artificially inflated by about ₹1,280 cr in FY19–FY20 by delaying impairments; money from preferential allottees did not show up or match bank statements — [BQ Prime](https://www.bqprime.com/business/sebi-unravels-how-brightcom-group-cooked-its-books); [SEBI order PDF (Feb 2025)](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/feb-2025/1738846203125_1.pdf)
- Penalties: ~₹34 cr total, including ₹15 cr each on promoters M. Suresh Kumar Reddy and Vijay Kancharla; Oct 2025 order penalised former independent directors (₹35 lakh) for failing fiduciary duties — [Storyboard18](https://www.storyboard18.com/digital/sebi-fines-brightcom-group-%E2%82%B934-crore-for-financial-misrepresentation-56014.htm); [Moneylife](https://www.moneylife.in/article/brightcom-group-sebi-slaps-rs35-lakh-penalty-on-2-exdirectors-for-accounting-irregularities/78509.html); [SEBI order PDF (Oct 2025)](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/oct-2025/1759753202973_1.pdf)
- Note: figures across reports differ (₹868 cr vs ~₹1,280–1,300 cr) depending on period/order — verify against the SEBI PDFs.

**Manpasand Beverages – auditor exits + fake invoicing**
- Deloitte resigned in May 2018 citing non-provision of "significant information"; second auditor Mehra Goel & Co quit July 2019 — [Moneylife](https://moneylife.in/article/after-deloitte-mehra-goel-co-resigns-as-manpasands-auditors/57645.html); [Business Standard](https://business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/gst-scam-manpasand-bev-s-auditor-resigns-stock-locked-in-5-lower-circuit-119071000226_1.html)
- MD Abhishek Singh, his brother and CFO arrested May 2019 in a ₹40 cr GST fake-invoice fraud using 30+ bogus units — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/current-affairs/manpasand-beverages-md-officials-arrested-in-rs-40-crore-gst-fraud-119052500241_1.html); [Business Standard explainer](https://business-standard.com/article/companies/how-gst-fraud-worth-rs-40-crore-came-into-light-at-manpasand-beverages-119053100023_1.html)

body: Many Indian multibaggers come from cycles more than from stock picking. Government capex and a revival of the private capex/order cycle re-rated capital goods and PSUs from depressed 2020 levels. Valuations then expanded until fund managers turned cautious in 2024. Cycles create multibaggers when you buy at trough earnings and trough multiples, and they destroy capital when you buy at peak multiples.

body:
`person:raamdeo-agrawal` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: india, process, quality, growth, base-rate

Co-founder (1987, with Motilal Oswal) of Motilal Oswal Financial Services; author of the annual Motilal Oswal Wealth Creation Study since 1996 - the longest-running Indian dataset on which stocks created wealth and why. Early notable investments: Hero Honda, Infosys and Eicher Motors; his personal portfolio reportedly grew to ~Rs 100 crore by 2000 (Wikipedia; single-source). Hero Honda ranked first among the most consistent wealth creators in the 12th study (2002-07); Infosys, Hero Honda and Ranbaxy appeared in ten straight studies. Folklore (unverified): a ~Rs 10 lakh Hero Honda investment in the early 1990s grew to many crores. Process: QGLP - Quality (business and management), Growth (earnings growth runway), Longevity (how long growth and returns last), Price (reasonable vs growth) - plus 'Size' (small at the start, per the 100x study). The studies' core finding: big wealth comes from earnings growth plus P/E rerating, and buying at low P/E relative to future growth. Mistakes: Motilal Oswal's flagship MF schemes lagged badly in 2018-2021 when their quality-growth holdings de-rated and they missed cyclicals/PSUs (characterisation; check fund data). Copyable: the study PDFs are free - use their stock-level tables as a base-rate library (what % of wealth creators were small, at what P/E they started).

1. FY19: 137 + 355 − 265 = **227 days**. FY20: 168 + 400 − 253 = **315 days** (matches Screener). Vendors carried roughly 250+ days of payables, and lenders rolled over about ₹11,500–13,200 cr of borrowings until the FY21 restructuring (borrowings then fell to 6,925). Survival depended on creditors, not customers.
2. DSO = 6,125/39,063×365 = **57.2 days**. DIO = 12,896/34,836×365 = **135 days**. DSO jumped 21 days in a year while revenue rose 78%, and CFO was −$6.8 bn. Either sales are being made on longer terms to win volume or collections are slipping. In either case, growth is being financed by SMCI's balance sheet. Feed this into Beneish's DSRI in Lesson 5.
3. Total DSO = (500 + 700)/2,000 × 365 = **219 days**. Net of advances: (1,200 − 200)/2,000 × 365 = **183 days**. Contract assets exceed billed receivables, so ask for the ageing of unbilled balances and for any arbitration claims included in them.

body:
| Area | Ind AS (≈ IFRS) | US GAAP | Adjust by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Leases (lessee) | Single model: depreciation + interest. CFO excludes lease cash | Operating leases: straight-line opex, cash in CFO | Deduct lease payments from Ind AS EBITDA and CFO (Lesson 4.6) |
| Interest paid in CFS | Operating or financing (choice) | Operating | Move interest into CFO |
| Development costs | Capitalised when criteria met (Ind AS 38) | Expensed (ASC 730), except some software | Add back capitalised development to expenses, or compare on cash R&D |
| PP&E revaluation | Allowed (revaluation model) | Prohibited | Check for revaluation reserves inflating book value and depressing ROE |
| Impairment reversal | Allowed (not for goodwill) | Prohibited | Watch "reversal of impairment" in other income |
| Inventory | LIFO prohibited | LIFO allowed | US LIFO firms: add the LIFO reserve to inventory and equity |
| Provisions | Recognise if probable (>50%) | Probable is a higher bar. Low end of range | Indian companies recognise more; US companies disclose more |
| "Exceptional items" | Separate line common (Schedule III) | No extraordinary items (ASU 2015-01). "Unusual or infrequent" in notes | Indian exceptionals deserve the recurrence test (5.2) |
| Bank overdraft | Can be part of cash & equivalents | Financing | Net cash looks higher under Ind AS |
| Componentisation | Required | Permitted, less common | Different depreciation profiles |
| Non-GAAP metrics | Little regulation (SEBI requires no reconciliation for "EBITDA") | Reg G / Item 10(e): reconciliation required | Rebuild Indian "adjusted EBITDA" yourself |
| Goodwill | Impairment only | Impairment only (private companies may amortise) | Same |
| Revenue | Ind AS 115 | ASC 606 | Converged. Ind AS 115 carve-outs are minor (e.g. penalties presentation) |
| Consolidation | Control model (Ind AS 110) | Voting-interest + VIE model | Check for unconsolidated "associates" holding debt |

body:
- PEAD is **public and well known**, so the edge is not the idea. Our edge is that in India it is still **operationally
  expensive to compute** (XBRL/PDF results, scattered dates, standalone vs consolidated, unit errors) and few retail investors
  do it systematically. The anomaly survives out of sample at t ≈ 4, unlike the US large/mid-cap market (Martineau 2022).
- **Practical long-only use (hypothesis-grade, not a trading system):**
  1. **Avoid or exit after a big negative SUE.** This is the most robust leg (−2.1% to −2.7%/quarter vs controls, t ≈ −4.5 in
     both periods), it costs nothing to apply, and it needs no shorting.
  2. **Tilt the research queue toward top-SUE names**, ideally ₹1,000–50,000 cr with a positive announcement reaction, and hold
     ~3–6 months. Expect roughly +2% per quarter vs same-size stocks before costs, and a skewed distribution (most single
     names lag; the basket wins). You need ~30 names to collect it reliably.
- It is **not a multibagger engine.** It is a quarterly-earnings timing and filtering layer that can sit on top of
  fundamental research (base rate: top-SUE stocks beat same-size peers ~47% of the time individually).
- Next tests (pre-register first): (a) consolidated EPS from FY2020; (b) the full universe; (c) the confirmed-reaction filter;
  (d) the 2026 quarters as fresh out-of-sample data, given the weak 2025 H1.
